title: You followed them…
paragraphs:
You followed them…
and slowly forgot Him.

Not overnight.
Not loudly.
Just… quietly.

At first, it felt right.
The sermons were powerful.
The words were sharp.
The presence… convincing.

But somewhere between admiration and attachment—
your eyes shifted.
And now you don’t even notice it.

You quote your favorite preacher more than Scripture.
You defend a leader faster than you examine your own heart.
You feel closer to a personality…
than to the presence of Jesus.
And here’s the dangerous part—
It still feels spiritual.
But is it?

Because Hebrews says, “looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith…” (Hebrews 12:2).
Not your pastor.
Not your priest.
Not your bishop.
Jesus.
So why do we drift?

Because it’s easier to follow someone visible
than surrender to Someone holy.

It’s easier to admire a voice
than obey the Word.
And sometimes… if we’re honest…

We hide behind spiritual leaders
so we don’t have to deal with our own secret compromise.
Yes.

That quiet sin you’ve been excusing.
That delayed obedience you keep postponing.
That pride that whispers, “I’m still okay.”
But Scripture cuts deeper than comfort.
Jeremiah 17:5 warns, “Cursed is the one who trusts in man… whose heart turns away from the Lord.”
Read that again.

This isn’t about dishonoring leaders.
This is about misplaced devotion.

Because when a man becomes your source,
God becomes your option.

And some of us—
we don’t worship pastors with songs…
we worship them with dependence.
That’s the kind of idolatry that looks like loyalty.

Let me ask you something—
When was the last time you opened your Bible… not to prepare a post, not to quote someone… but to hear Jesus speak to you?
When was the last time His voice alone convicted you… without a sermon, without a stage, without a screen?
Or have you slowly replaced encounter… with content?
This might be why your spirit feels dry.

Not because God stopped speaking—
but because you stopped looking at Him.
AHA REVELATION:

You don’t lose faith in a moment—
you lose focus in inches.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

If your faith collapses when a leader fails,
it reveals where your foundation was built.
And here’s the truth that cuts—

Some people know church culture…
but don’t know Christ.

You can serve in ministry
and still be distant from Jesus.

You can preach truth
and still avoid surrender.

You can look anointed
and still be unrepentant.
But here’s where grace walks in.

Jesus never asked you to be perfect—
He asked you to come.

Come broken.
Come distracted.
Come misaligned.

Because the same verse that calls Him the author of your faith…
also calls Him the finisher.
Meaning—

Even if you’ve drifted…
He’s not done.

Even if you misplaced your focus…
He can realign your heart.
But it requires something we don’t like to talk about:
Repentance.

Not guilt.
Not shame.
Repentance.
A turning.
Acts 3:19 says, “Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out…”

Not managed.
Not hidden.
Blotted out.
Through Jesus.

Not through your pastor.
Not through your good works.
Not through your church attendance.
Only Christ.

The cross was never shared.
Salvation was never delegated.
It is finished—by Him alone.
So here’s the invitation—
Come back.

Not to religion.
Not to routine.
Not to performance.
Come back to Jesus.

Let Him be your focus again.
Let Him be your voice again.
Let Him be your Savior again.
And if you’re hungry to go deeper—
Because borrowed faith won’t survive real storms.
But a Christ-centered life?
Unshakable.
If this exposed something in you… don’t ignore it.
And the next message?
It might confront the one thing you’ve been avoiding.
